vibe.content:
🎵 SLOW JAM: The Heights, "How Do You Talk to an Angel" (1992)
• No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 (Nov. 14, 1992 chart, two weeks); it ended Boyz II Men's record 13-week run at the top with "End of the Road" and was knocked off by Whitney Houston's "I Will Always Love You"
• The Heights was a fictional band on a Fox drama of the same name; actor Jamie Walters sang lead and Brandon Fields played the sax. The show was canceled about a week after the song fell from No. 1.
• Why today: it was the No. 1 song in America this very week 34 years ago, and it's the softest start to a Thursday we've got.
😂 JOKES: A No. 1 hit from a TV show nobody watched. That might be the most 90s sentence ever written. / Great sax solo. Honestly, the saxophone did more work than the TV show.

🚗 DRIVE TEASE: About 54 and clear for the drive in, dry roads, then mostly sunny and up near 63 this afternoon with a southwest wind 10 to 15 and gusts up to 35. Beitner Bridge reopened Wednesday afternoon, and MDOT retimes the Chums Corner light today.
😂 JOKES: It's 63 and sunny in November, with gusts to 35. Your hair has an opinion about it. / The Beitner Bridge is open and the Chums Corner light gets fixed today. For once the drive is the good news.
📅 THIS DAY: On this day in 1969, Apollo 12 landed in the Moon's Ocean of Storms. Pete Conrad and Alan Bean touched down within walking distance of Surveyor 3, a robotic probe that landed there in 1967.
😂 JOKES: Apollo 12 landed so close to its target that the astronauts could walk to a probe that had been sitting there since 1967. My GPS can't get me to Meijer that well. / They survived two lightning strikes on launch and still landed on the dime. And I get nervous when my phone is at 4 percent.
💡 FUN FACT: GTA 6 is at 99 out of 100 on Metacritic from 150 critic reviews, tying Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the highest score the site has listed.
😂 JOKES: A 99 on Metacritic. I've never gotten a 99 on anything, unless it's my age on a bad Monday. / Ocarina of Time held that 99 all by itself for 28 years. Vice City just walked in and sat down next to it.
🎉 NATIONAL DAYS: National Play Monopoly Day, National Carbonated Beverage with Caffeine Day, International Men's Day and National Rural Health Day
😂 JOKES: National Play Monopoly Day: the only day it's legal to bankrupt your family and still make it to Thanksgiving dinner. / Carbonated Beverage with Caffeine Day. The day after GTA 6, that's just called Thursday.

☀️ 54 and clear at the airport at 6 AM, then mostly sunny with a high near 63, SW wind 10-15 with gusts to 35, a low near 41 tonight, partly sunny and 61 Friday, 65 Saturday, then rain showers Sunday.
🚧 Beitner Bridge is open; MDOT retimes the Chums Corner light today and the temporary Hartman Road light comes out Friday morning.
⚡ It's 63 in November, GTA 6 is out, and a Marine recruiter is in the studio at 7:30. Thursday came to play.

mood.content:
Wham!, "Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go" (1984)
• Wham!'s first UK and first US No. 1; three weeks at the top of the Billboard Hot 100 and platinum in the US
• The story: the title came from a note Andrew Ridgeley left for his parents that was meant to read "wake me up before you go" but had "up" written twice, so he made the "go" double on purpose. George Michael wrote and produced it, and the band recorded it in two days.
• Why today: it's Thursday, it's National Carbonated Beverage with Caffeine Day, and it's 63 and sunny. Perfect pick-me-up for after 6:30.
😂 JOKES: Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go and National Carbonated Beverage with Caffeine Day on the same morning. The universe is trying to tell us something. / I told my alarm 'wake me up before you go-go' and it just went-went without me.

⭐ TOP STORY: KINGSLEY STAGS: UNBEATEN VS. UNBEATEN FOR A TRIP TO FORD FIELD
SUMMARY: Kingsley and Almont are both 12-0 and meet Saturday at 1 PM in Clare in the Division 6 state semifinal. The winner plays for the Division 6 title at Ford Field on Friday, Nov. 27.
KEY POINTS:
• WHO: Kingsley Stags (12-0) vs. Almont Raiders (12-0)
• WHAT: Division 6 state semifinal; the winner plays for the Division 6 title. Tickets listed at $12 on GoFan.
• WHERE: Brookwood Athletic Complex, Clare High School (final: Ford Field, Detroit)
• WHEN: Saturday, Nov. 21, 1 PM (final: Friday, Nov. 27, 4 PM)
• WHY: Both won regional finals last Friday: Kingsley 34-28 over Sanford-Meridian in the snow (Perry Smith's 13-yard TD with 39 seconds left, per MLive) and Almont 41-14 over Marine City. The winner goes to Ford Field.
➜ THE CATCH/TWIST: The teams are nearly mirror images: Almont has outscored opponents 481-198 (40 a game, 16.5 allowed) and Kingsley 489 (41 a game, 15 allowed). Almont's two closest wins were 14-13 and 28-27; Kingsley's only real regular-season test was a 46-41 win over Haslett. It's also a rematch of the 2023 state final, which Kingsley won 38-24.
➜ THE TAKE: Same record, same scoring, one perfect season left. The Stags already beat Almont for the 2023 state title, so go Stags, and bring a coat.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: are you making the drive to Clare Saturday? Give us your Stags score prediction.
😂 JOKES: Twelve and oh versus twelve and oh. Somebody's perfect season ends Saturday, and it's not gonna be ours, Stags. / Kingsley beat Sanford-Meridian in the snow. Clare in November? They're ready for anything.

⭐ TOP STORY: BEITNER BRIDGE IS OPEN, AND TODAY THE CHUMS CORNER LIGHT GETS RETIMED
SUMMARY: The Beitner Bridge reopened to cars Wednesday afternoon, but rush-hour traffic backed up near Chums Corner because the light was never retimed for it. MDOT says it changes the signal timing today.
KEY POINTS:
• WHO: Grand Traverse County Road Commission (bridge); MDOT (the signals, spokesman James Lake)
• WHAT: Beitner Bridge reopened to vehicle traffic; MDOT will 'change that signal timing' at US-31/M-37/Beitner; the detour's temporary light at US-31/Hartman comes out Friday
• WHERE: Beitner Road bridge and Chums Corner (US-31/M-37/Beitner); temporary light at US-31/Hartman Road
• WHEN: Reopened Wednesday shortly before 3 PM; signal change Thursday (today); temporary light removed starting 9 AM Friday, finished by end of day, with delays expected at US-31/Hartman
• WHY: The light hadn't been adjusted to reflect the bridge reopening, so a short green backed traffic up at rush hour.
➜ THE CATCH/TWIST: The Road Commission held the ribbon cutting Tuesday without knowing when the bridge would actually open. It opened Wednesday, and the US-31/M-37/Beitner light hadn't been adjusted, so only a handful of cars got through each short green.
➜ THE TAKE: After all that waiting for a bridge, the first thing it got was a traffic jam. Welcome back, Beitner. Plan on Chums Corner being tight until MDOT finishes the retime (the article gives no time).
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: did you try the Beitner Bridge last night, and how bad was Chums Corner?
😂 JOKES: After all that waiting, the bridge reopened and the first thing it got was a traffic jam. Welcome back, Beitner. / Nothing says a fresh start like a green light that lasts four seconds.

⭐ TOP STORY: A MOBILE ER DOCTOR IS RIDING TO 911 CALLS IN NORTHWEST MICHIGAN
SUMMARY: Dr. Shaun Ramsey drives a Munson-backed EMS physician response vehicle that brings an emergency doctor to the scene of 911 calls in northwest Michigan, where transport times can be long.
KEY POINTS:
• WHO: Dr. Shaun C. Ramsey, DO, Northwest Regional Medical Control Authority, with support from Munson Healthcare
• WHAT: An EMS physician response vehicle: a physician with a larger scope than an EMT or paramedic, who can give medicines and do procedures they can't
• WHERE: Rural northwest Michigan, at the scene of car accidents or in someone's home
• WHEN: Ramsey has been in the role for 11 months (UpNorthLive, Nov. 17)
• WHY: Transport times are long in a rural setting, and minutes and sometimes seconds matter, so physician-level care starts on scene.
➜ THE CATCH/TWIST: He is the only EMS physician north of Saginaw, and there are only a few in the whole state. He listens to incoming 911 calls and, based on how serious and how close, decides whether to hit the lights and sirens and respond.
➜ THE TAKE: Your 911 call can now get a doctor on scene with lights and sirens. House calls are back.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: have you ever needed 911 Up North, and how fast did help get there?
😂 JOKES: A doctor who makes house calls, with lights and sirens. My doctor can't even make a same-week appointment. / Finally, a doctor who comes to you, and he brings his own siren.

⭐ TOP STORY: FRANKFORT SAYS YES TO IRONMAN IN 2027, WITH A MARCH CHECK-IN
SUMMARY: Frankfort City Council voted Monday night to bring Ironman Michigan back in 2027. Key contingencies come back in March, along with a vote on a three-year contract.
KEY POINTS:
• WHO: Frankfort City Council and Mayor JoAnn Holwerda; Ironman Michigan
• WHAT: Council voted to move forward with the 2027 race with a few changes to its structure; contingencies get re-evaluated in March
• WHERE: Frankfort City Hall, Benzie County, standing room only
• WHEN: Vote Monday night (Nov. 16); next decision at the March council meeting
• WHY: Most public speakers cited the tourism boost the race brings past Labor Day; some council members relayed concerns about parking and businesses hurt by the race. The mayor: 'This last year was just phenomenal.'
➜ THE CATCH/TWIST: The yes isn't forever. In March the council also decides whether to sign a three-year contract or make 2027 Ironman's last stop in Frankfort, and some council members raised parking and business-impact concerns.
➜ THE TAKE: Standing room only to vote on a race where everyone else has to do the running.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: would you do an Ironman, or just stand on the curb with a sign?
😂 JOKES: Frankfort filled City Hall to vote on Ironman. Meanwhile I can't get a family vote on where to eat. / Swim, bike, run a marathon. Or as my family calls it, Thanksgiving prep.

━━ MORE LOCAL ━━

INLAND SEAS HITS 200,000 STUDENTS AND ADULTS ON THE GREAT LAKES
• The Suttons Bay nonprofit reached 200,000 total participants in its 37th year; it was founded in 1989.
• The first 100,000 took 25 years; the second 100,000 took 12.
• The milestone class was from Suttons Bay Public Schools, learning paper maps and compasses on shore.
• Two tall-ship schooners, the Inland Seas and the Alliance, carry students out to collect science data. Skyler Singleton: 'Once you know the lakes in this region, you end up falling in love with it.'
➜ TAKE: Two hundred thousand people and a compass. Somebody taught a generation to find north without a phone.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: did you ever sail on a schooner or take a Great Lakes class as a kid?
😂 JOKES: Two hundred thousand students and they're still teaching paper maps. A paper map never says 'recalculating.' / Reading a compass: the original GPS, and it never needed a software update. Unlike some games I could mention.

GLEN ARBOR LIGHTS UP 20+ TREES FOR TEENS (YOU CAN SPONSOR ONE)
• The Strolling Lights Festival in downtown Glen Arbor has 20+ decorated trees; this year it benefits LIFT (Leelanau Investing for Teens).
• LIFT is a free out-of-school program for grades 6-12 in the Glen Lake, Suttons Bay, Leland and Northport schools, with daily mentoring and homework help; it has helped well over 1,000 teens since 2017.
• Sponsoring a tree is $150 (CrystalRiverOutfitters.com/strolling-lights-festival), and you can also donate to LIFT without decorating one.
• Decorating starts Saturday, Nov. 21; trees are up Thanksgiving weekend through New Year's.
➜ TAKE: A decorating committee where every tree gets to look different and nobody argues about the star.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the best Christmas tree you ever decorated, or the worst?
😂 JOKES: Twenty trees, twenty decorators, zero arguments about who puts on the star. Glen Arbor is doing the holidays right. / A hundred and fifty bucks buys a tree. At my house it buys the tree stand and an argument.

items.title: INLAND SEAS HITS 200,000 STUDENTS AND ADULTS ON THE GREAT LAKES
items.recap: We covered Inland Seas Education Association reaching 200,000 participants in 37 years.
items.description: The Inland Seas Education Association in Suttons Bay has reached 200,000 total participants across its Great Lakes science and sailing programs, in its 37th year. It took 25 years to reach the first 100,000 and just 12 more to double it. The milestone group was a Suttons Bay Public Schools class doing an onshore watershed program, reading paper maps and using compasses. The nonprofit runs two traditionally rigged schooners, the Inland Seas and the Alliance, and its programs reach students from Suttons Bay, Elk Rapids, Petoskey and Cadillac to Grand Rapids and Detroit.

• Two tall-ship schooners, the Inland Seas and the Alliance, carry students out to collect science data. Skyler Singleton: 'Once you know the lakes in this region, you end up falling in love with it.'

gta6.title: GTA 6 Watch
gta6.content:
⭐ TOP STORY: GTA 6 WATCH
SUMMARY: Grand Theft Auto VI is out today after a 13-year wait, with 99 out of 100 on Metacritic from 150 critics. NBC says gamers are skipping work to play.
KEY POINTS:
• WHO: Rockstar Games; players follow Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, the first female lead in a GTA game, and you can toggle between them
• WHAT: GTA VI released: 99/100 on Metacritic, about 16 million copies and $1.5 billion+ in prelaunch sales (Sensor Tower), and a field-leading 8 Game Awards nominations
• WHERE: Vice City, in the fictional state of Leonida (inspired by Miami and Florida); New Zealand got it first, and Miami held a 'Vice City' night at the Heat-Bucks game
• WHEN: Today, Nov. 19 (The Game Awards are Dec. 10)
• WHY: It's the first main GTA game in 13 years, the longest gap in the series, and critics are calling it a 'masterpiece'.
➜ THE CATCH/TWIST: NBC's warning: finishing the game's 100 missions will take around 50 hours (per Insider Gaming), so don't be surprised if loved ones or employees are hard to reach today.
➜ THE TAKE: For the first time in 13 years the wait was the easy part. Now the hard part is explaining Thursday to your boss.
😂 JOKES: Thirteen years of waiting and the first score is a 99. Even my mom never gave me a 99. / A 212-gigabyte download, a firmware update and a day-one patch. That's not a video game, that's a lease.

━━ MORE GTA 6 ━━

GTA 6 WATCH: IT'S OUT NOW
• CONFIRMED: Grand Theft Auto VI unlocked at midnight local time on Nov. 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, country by country starting with New Zealand; in the US it was one moment, 12 AM ET. Single-player at launch; no PC version until 2027
• NEW: Reviews are near-perfect: 99 out of 100 on Metacritic from 150 critics, tying Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the highest ever. IGN and GameSpot gave 10/10, Eurogamer 5/5; the lowest is an 80. That confirms the fan's '99 on Metacritic' claim in the ABC clip (c01)
• NEW: About 16 million copies and $1.5 billion in prelaunch sales (Sensor Tower via NBC News). A later Sensor Tower estimate is about 17 million, roughly 75% on PlayStation (estimate)
• PRICE: $79.99 Standard, $99.99 Ultimate (digital only); the box is a download code, and the download is about 212 GB. PS5 needed system update 14.23.00 (about 1.2 GB) plus a 602 MB day-one patch
• PLAYER REPORTS (not Rockstar): early glitches and frame-rate dips on base PS5; PeakMetrics says posts about stutter jumped about 55 times a normal day. mental.title: Mental Health Minute
mental.content:
"Name It to Tame It"

It's the Thursday before Thanksgiving week, the sun is out, and a lot of us are already carrying the to-do list, the travel plans and the family math in our heads. So here's a thirty-second trick for when your stomach tightens. Stop and name the feeling in one or two words, out loud or on your phone, like 'I'm anxious,' or 'I'm frustrated,' or 'I'm overwhelmed.' That's it. Researchers at UCLA scanned people's brains while they looked at upsetting images, and when people put a word on the emotion, activity in the amygdala, the brain's alarm system, went down, and activity in a part of the prefrontal cortex that helps regulate emotion went up. In plain English: saying what you feel can turn the volume down. It's not a cure and it's not therapy, it's just a small move you can make in a parking lot, a grocery line or a hallway. So today, the next time the stress spikes, name it. And if you want to share what you named, text the studio at 231-929-4487.
mental.notes: Evidence: Lieberman, Eisenberger, Crockett, Tom, Pfeifer & Way (2007), Psychological Science 18(5): labeling emotion reduced amygdala/limbic response and increased right ventrolateral prefrontal activity. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17576282/ ; full text https://sanlab.psych.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/31/2016/03/Lieberman_2007_PsychScience.pdf . Not a clinical claim. Fresh this week. ~60 s.
